<reason>Both sides were competent and well-grounded, but B edged the decisive clashes. B answered A's pressure questions honestly and effectively: on frictionless consent, B conceded the regime and defended low opt-in via rational ignorance over pennies of value, converting A's trap into a proportionality argument that presumptive illegality is law's strongest medicine, disproportionate to a trivially-valued exchange. B's "three statutes from the podium" meta-argument exposed real line-drawing drift in A's case (non-tracking tier, self-defined scale threshold, network-pays cost allocation), and A's reply that this is ordinary statutory construction was only partially persuasive. Critically, B's economic stake — that contextual yields are far lower, so the real choice is a thinner, paywalled internet — was asserted by A to be false but never seriously rebutted. A landed strong counterpunches: the "stranger lifting a penny from every pocket" retort, the collective-action explanation for why opt-out fails, and clean A1/A2 answers with a defensible cross-context line. But A's core dilemma response ("yeses will come; if not, nothing of value is lost") left one horn exposed, since B's yield-gap claim meant the free internet could die without any consent failure. B's Rebuttal 2 was clipped, a real execution cost, but its visible content still delivered the debate's sharpest weighing. Narrow but clear B win on better pressure handling and unanswered proportionality/economics.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's answer to A's frictionless-consent pressure question (B4.1): rather than dodging, B accepted the one-click regime and argued low opt-in reflects rational ignorance over fractions of a cent, which B then weaponized in closing — a presumption of illegality is disproportionate to conduct each victim values at pennies. A's best exchange was the mirror image: recasting B's own "pennies and friction" account as proof that individuals cannot carry the enforcement burden, hence the need for an ex ante default ("a stranger may not lift a penny from every pocket and call objection friction").</best_rebuttal>
